data.content_ref: inline:The target falsely claims that no autonomous reclamation protocol can guarantee never to silently displace completed evidence. A conservative autonomous protocol that simply declines to reclaim any workspace lacking a terminal record (or a durable, locally-verifiable evacuation manifest) trivially satisfies the guarantee by never acting on ambiguous workspaces. The problem asks for the safest protocol and the durable record it must keep, not for throughput or bounded resource use, so autonomy is not a barrier to safety. By insisting an external adjudicator is necessary, the target misdiagnoses the problem, introduces an avoidable unbounded-delay dependency (countercondition 1), and fails to identify the actual safest autonomous answer. Moreover, the proposed adjudicator itself cannot overcome observational equivalence when checkpoints omit the final transition (countercondition 2), so the external mechanism does not achieve the guarantee the target treats as out of reach for autonomous systems.
